validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all clear. This row is FERC Docket CP19-512-000, Texas Eastern Transmission LP's 'Cameron Expansion Project' (the applicant's own filing name, matching the sheet's segment_name exactly) -- an interstate NGA Sec.7(c) compression + interconnect project on Texas Eastern's existing Line 41 mainline in Beauregard/Calcasieu/Cameron/Jefferson Davis parishes, LA, delivering feedgas to Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass LNG terminal. Independently confirmed real and built via FERC's own environmental assessment (elibrary/ferc.gov EA PDF), the Federal Register notice of the Sept 26 2019 application, EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset (24 vintages, 2019-10 through 2026-08, tracking it Applied->Approved->Part Completed->Completed, completed_date 2021-12-09), EIA's own 'Today in Energy' feature (Nov 2021, names the project directly), and Pipeline & Gas Journal trade press (Sep 14 2021). No duplicate: checked against the 41-row roster -- P2518 'Texas Gas Transmission Pipeline' is a wholly different company (Boardwalk-owned Texas Gas Transmission, not Enbridge's Texas Eastern Transmission) despite the similar name; no other row references Line 41 or the Cameron Extension/Expansion project. Classification (transmission, Gas) confirmed by the same NGA Sec.7(c) certificate proceeding, which only interstate transmission pipelines require. TWO SPEC ISSUES found: (1) DIAMETER -- the original Sept 2019 application and the Federal Register notice (which the sheet's current 20.00 in figure and EIA's stale spreadsheet entry both trace to) proposed '0.2 miles of 20-inch-diameter interconnecting piping,' but FERC's own environmental assessment (issued 2020-04, docket CP19-512-EA.pdf, pp.443/453) describes the same 0.2-mile segment as '30-inch-diameter,' and Pipeline & Gas Journal's Sep 2021 nearing-completion story (sourced to an Enbridge spokesperson, describing the as-built project) also states '0.2 miles of 30-inch diameter interconnecting piping.' Two independent, later-dated sources (FERC's EA and Enbridge/PGJ) agree the built pipe is 30-inch, evidently enlarged from the original 20-inch application during FERC review; EIA's spreadsheet was never updated off the original filing figure. Filed as a fills[] REFS_ADDED correction to 30.00 in below. (2) DELAY -- the sheet records Delayed=yes/DelayType=inferred, but PGJ (Sep 2021, quoting Enbridge) states the November 2021 target in-service date is 'right on schedule' against Enbridge's own prediction that construction would finish in H2 2021, and EIA's dataset shows the same target in-service year (2021) unchanged across every vintage from the 2019-10 filing through actual completion (2021-12-09) -- i.e. it finished within its originally projected year. No source found describing any delay, schedule slip, or FERC-ordered extension. Recommend Delayed=no/DelayType=blank pending a source that actually documents a delay.
